learning_outcomes.text: Knowledge in basic and technological subjects, enabling them to learn new methods and theories, and providing them with versatility to adapt to new situations.

Ability to solve problems with initiative, decision-making, creativity, critical reasoning, and to communicate and transmit knowledge, skills, and abilities in the field of Industrial Engineering, specific mechanical technology.
Knowledge for performing measurements, calculations, valuations, appraisals, expert reports, studies, reports, work plans, and other similar tasks.
Ability to handle specifications, regulations, and mandatory standards.
Ability to apply quality principles and methods.
Ability to work in a multilingual and multidisciplinary environment.

Apply the strategies of the scientific methodology: analyze the problematic situation qualitatively and quantitatively, propose hypotheses and solutions using the models typical of industrial engineering, mechanical specialty.
Basic knowledge of production and manufacturing systems.
Perform dimensional verification of parts based on their specifications and the properties of the measuring instrument.
Distinguish the fundamental characteristics of different manufacturing processes based on their field of application.
Know and identify the main welding processes and be able to estimate their costs.
Know and identify the different sand molding processes, understanding the main advantages and disadvantages depending on the type of part to be manufactured.
Know the main plastic metal forming processes, such as forging, extrusion, and sheet metal forming, identifying their main variables.
Know the main machining processes and delve into calculations related to operations.
Perform cost calculations in machining operations with the objective of establishing optimal process conditions.
Acquire basic knowledge of CNC programming and understand the functioning of a CNC system as a whole.

assessment_rules: There are two evaluation modes: continuous and final. By default, all students will follow continuous evaluation. To opt for final evaluation, students must notify the lecturer within the first 9 weeks of the semester. For continuous evaluation, content is assessed in three parts: topics 1-8 (40%), topics 9-13 (30%), and practicals (30%). A minimum score of 4.5 out of 10 is required in each of these three parts, and the weighted average must be 5 or higher to pass. If a student scores 4.5 or higher in any of the first two parts (practicals or theoretical content of topics 1-8), that part is released and does not need to be re-examined in the ordinary call. For final evaluation and the extraordinary call, all concepts from theoretical and practical classes are examined, and a weighted average of 5 or higher is required to pass.
